dramatic_tail.example: Y: 'Will Karen and Veletian have a formal peace in effect at turn 180?' (q~0.01); X: 'Karen and Veletian reached a cease-fire (turns 61-90)' -> p(Y|X) mid-band

conditional_continuous.design: turn 1: percentiles for a count question; turn 2: 61-90 event reveal, re-elicit percentiles; truth = conditional distribution over half-B rollouts where X holds (n_x>=100); score CRPS vs conditional distribution and excess over the perfect conditional forecaster
conditional_continuous.nesting: label pairs as NESTED (the revealed event is itself part of the counted quantity - mechanical shift, a sanity check the model must at least match) vs NON-NESTED (momentum/spillover - the real test); include both, ~half each
conditional_continuous.example: Y: 'How many cities will Songhai capture by turn 180?'; X nested: 'Songhai captured a city (61-90)'; X non-nested: 'Karen lost a city to Crimean Tatar (61-90)'

no_news.text: turn 2: 'The game has continued. No new information about turns 60-90 is available. If you wish, revise your forecast...'
no_news.measures: drift/noise floor - movement with zero information; natcond updates are judged against it; branches off the shared turn-1 (turn-2 cost only)

single_turn.text: one prompt: report + revealed fact inserted before the criteria (fact sentence word-identical to the turn-2 opener)
single_turn.measures: anchoring on one's own turn-1 answer: two-turn p2 vs single-turn p isolates conversational structure; fresh full prompt cost

controls.null_stratum_vs_no_news: distinct: null stratum = real news with ~zero effect (selectivity); no-news = no news at all (stability)
